headline: NVIDIA Vera Rubin 800V power mandate triggers data-center power redesign; Taiwan power duo Delta & Lite-On positioned
headline_zh: 輝達 Vera Rubin 電力硬規：800V 變革啟動，台廠電源雙雄台達電、光寶科的千金行情布局
source_label: 永豐金證券 豐雲學堂 (SinoPac RichClub)
bull_case: The Vera Rubin platform forces a structural rewrite of data-center power: in-rack distribution moves from 54V to 800V HVDC to feed racks scaling from ~130kW (NVL144) toward 600kW–1MW (Rubin Ultra Kyber, 2027). NVIDIA's own Oct-2025 800VDC announcement enrolled 50+ partners and explicitly listed Delta and LITEON in the power/cooling-integration tier — independent confirmation that the article's '電源雙雄' framing is real, not promotional. The value-capture story is the upgrade: vendors shift from selling discrete components (connectors, BBU, SST) to delivering full rack-level power cabinets, lifting ASP and content-per-rack by an order of magnitude. 800V cuts copper losses (>150% more power through the same conductor vs 54V), trims TCO ~20-30%, and is mandatory — not optional — for Kyber-scale density, so demand is platform-gated rather than discretionary. Delta guides Q3-2026 mass production, aligning supply with NVIDIA's 2H-2026 first Vera Rubin shipments. US-listed power names (Vertiv, Eaton, Navitas, onsemi, Infineon, Power Integrations) ride the same secular 800VDC capex wave, giving the theme a deep, cross-listed beneficiary set rather than a single-name bet.
bear_case: Most of the headline power number belongs to the wrong product. Multiple independent sources put standard Vera Rubin NVL144 at ~120-130kW per rack; the 600kW figure is Rubin Ultra / Kyber, slated for 2H-2027 — so the article's '600kW Vera Rubin' framing front-loads a 2027 catalyst into a 2026 trade and risks a timing air-pocket. The 800VDC ecosystem is crowded and Western-anchored: NVIDIA's reference partners lead with Vertiv, Eaton, ABB, Schneider, Siemens, GE Vernova and silicon from Infineon/Navitas/onsemi/TI — Delta and Lite-On are two names among 50+, and the cnesa industry-chain list (31 firms) names Delta but omits Lite-On entirely, undercutting the clean 'duopoly moat' thesis. 'Full-cabinet solution delivery' raises integration, warranty and working-capital intensity, compressing the margin uplift the bull case assumes. The names have already run hard ('千金行情' = four-digit TWD price), so much of the 800V transition may be discounted; any Rubin Ultra slip, liquid-cooling bottleneck, or hyperscaler capex digestion hits richly-valued stocks first. This is a Taiwan-equity (2308.TW/2301.TW) story with no direct US-listed read-through for the duo themselves.
sector_view: Sector: Information Technology (power electronics / data-center infrastructure), bullish; Industrials (electrical equipment) bullish via Vertiv/Eaton/ABB/Schneider. Two-stage supply chain — UPSTREAM beneficiaries: power-semi (Navitas GaN/SiC, Infineon, onsemi, TI, Power Integrations) and SST/BBU/connector makers feed the 800V conversion stack; MIDSTREAM integrators: Delta (2308.TW) and Lite-On (2301.TW) plus Vertiv (VRT), Eaton (ETN) package rack-level HVDC power cabinets. DOWNSTREAM customer: NVIDIA (NVDA) sets the 800V spec and pulls demand; hyperscalers/neoclouds (Oracle, CoreWeave, Microsoft) are the end-buyers of the racks. WHO IS HURT: legacy 54V in-rack PSU vendors and AC-distribution incumbents face obsolescence as the 13.8kV-AC→800V-HVDC perimeter conversion eliminates AC/DC stages. Net: a content-expansion event for power-electronics names tied to NVIDIA's roadmap, with the directed edges NVDA←(supplies)←VRT/ETN/NVTS being the cross-listed expression of the Taiwan duo story.
macro_view: Macro-neutral, secular-positive. The driver is AI-capex intensity, not the rate cycle — data-center power buildout is a multi-year structural spend largely insensitive to near-term Fed path, though a higher-for-longer regime pressures the rich multiples these '千金' names carry (long-duration growth equities). FX: a stronger TWD would dent Delta/Lite-On reported margins (USD-denominated revenue, TWD cost base); USD strength is a mild tailwind. Historical analogue: the 54V→800V shift rhymes with prior platform-power step-changes (e.g. the move to 48V in-rack a cycle ago) where the spec-setter (NVIDIA) captured the roadmap and a handful of power-integration incumbents captured the content — early movers compounded, latecomers commoditized. Risk to the analogue: power/grid and liquid-cooling buildout, not silicon, is increasingly the binding constraint on AI scaling, which raises execution risk on the 2027 Kyber timeline the bull case leans on.
arbiter_reasoning: Verdict BULLISH, net_impact +2.6. The core claim survives cross-examination: NVIDIA's 800V HVDC mandate is real, platform-gated, and independently documented (Electronics Weekly, Oct-2025) to include both Delta and LITEON among 50+ named 800VDC partners, with Delta further confirmed by the cnesa 31-firm industry-chain list. The transition from 54V to 800V is mandatory for Rubin-class rack density (>150% more power through the same copper, ~20-30% TCO reduction), so the demand is structural rather than discretionary, and the component→full-cabinet shift is a genuine ASP/content-expansion lever. Two material caveats cap the score below +3.5. First, a timing/labeling issue: the eye-catching 600kW–1MW figures belong to Rubin Ultra / Kyber (2H-2027), while standard Vera Rubin NVL144 racks are ~120-130kW (2H-2026) — the article conflates them, so the biggest power numbers are a 2027 story being priced in 2026. Second, the 'duopoly moat' is overstated: the ecosystem is crowded and Western-led (Vertiv, Eaton, ABB, Schneider, Infineon, Navitas, onsemi), and one corroborating source names Delta but not Lite-On. The names have already re-rated ('千金行情'), so reward is increasingly execution- and timeline-dependent. Net: a real, multi-year content-expansion theme with a credible near-term (Q3-2026 Delta MP, 2H-2026 Vera Rubin) anchor, discounted for crowded competition and a partly front-loaded 2027 catalyst. This is an exploration-layer read and does not feed investment_protocol decisions.
debate_note: Bull sees a platform-mandated 800V content-expansion duopoly; bear says the 600kW 'duopoly' headline is a 2027 Rubin-Ultra story in a crowded Western-led field, front-loaded into already-re-rated 2026 prices.
